entry_points.name: close_account
entry_points.note: Sets deleted_at on the user row and commits; no row is removed here.

stores.name: users

fields.name: deleted_at
fields.note: Soft-delete marker written by close_account and read by the purge job.

erasure.note: close_account only writes deleted_at; the scheduled task purge_closed_accounts deletes user rows whose deleted_at is older than RETENTION_DAYS, and config.py schedules that task nightly.

stores.note: Table of account holders defined in models.py.

stores.name: invoices

fields.name: reference
fields.note: A comment on this column states the purge job does not touch this table.

erasure.note: The User.invoices relationship carries no cascade= string, so the ORM delete in the purge job does not propagate; the only delete path is the database-level ondelete="CASCADE", and the SQLite engine URL has no PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON listener in this repository, so whether foreign keys are enforced cannot be read from the source.

stores.note: Invoice table carrying a user_id foreign key to users.

stores.name: nightly_backup

fields.name: email
fields.note: Listed in DUMP_COLUMNS and read off each User row into the dump file.

fields.name: full_name
fields.note: Listed in DUMP_COLUMNS and read off each User row into the dump file.

fields.name: reference
fields.note: Listed in DUMP_COLUMNS and read off each Invoice row into the dump file.

erasure.note: The module carries a retention constant of 35 days and a cron string, and dump_database rewrites the file; no code in this repository reads BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS or deletes the dump.

stores.note: JSON dump of the users and invoices tables written to nightly_backup.json.
